name: Turkish Delight
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Soak 1 oz. gelatine in 1/2 cup of cold water for two hours
Put 1 pound of granulated sugar in a pan with 1/2 cup of cold water
Stand the pan over the fire until the sugar is melted and comes to the boil
Add soaked gelatine and boil steadily for twenty minutes
Flavor with the juice of one lemon and one orange and a tablespoonful of rum
Wet a tin in cold water and turn the mixture in, having it about one inch thick
When it is hard or jellied, spread icing sugar over the top and cut into inch square pieces
Let the mixture stand in the pan over night before cutting, as it is very sticky

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Soak 1 oz. gelatine in 1/2 cup of cold water for two hours
2. Put 1 pound of granulated sugar in a pan with 1/2 cup of cold water
3. Stand the pan over the fire until the sugar is melted and comes to the boil
4. Add soaked gelatine and boil steadily for twenty minutes
5. Flavor with the juice of one lemon and one orange and a tablespoonful of rum
6. Wet a tin in cold water and turn the mixture in, having it about one inch thick
7. When it is hard or jellied, spread icing sugar over the top and cut into inch square pieces
8. Roll in the icing sugar
9. Let the mixture stand in the pan over night before cutting, as it is very sticky
